title: Grade 4 One-Step Equations
seo_title: Grade 4 One-Step Equations Worksheets: Free Math with Answer Key (BC Curriculum)
standard_text: One-step equations with an unknown number, using all operations
meta_desc: Free Grade 4 math worksheets on one-step equations for the BC curriculum: the equal sign as a balance, unknowns like □ + 36 = 90, 4 × □ = 28 and n ÷ 3 = 6, writing equations for stories and word problems. 100 questions with an answer key, good FSA practice.
key_big: Use the inverse to find the unknown: subtraction undoes addition, and division undoes multiplication.
key_sub: 4 × □ = 28, so □ = 28 ÷ 4 = 7. n ÷ 3 = 6, so n = 6 × 3 = 18. The = sign means “is the same as”.
body_html:
The equal sign means “the same as”

An equation has an = sign. The = sign does not mean “the answer comes next”. It means both sides have the same value, like a pan balance that is level.

Find the unknown: use the inverse

A box □ or a letter like n stands for an unknown number. To find it, use the inverse operation, the one that undoes it. Then put your answer back in to check.

EquationUndo it withDo thisAnswer
□ + 36 = 90−90 − 3654
□ − 28 = 46+46 + 2874
4 × □ = 28÷28 ÷ 47
n ÷ 3 = 6×6 × 3n = 18
Example

n ÷ 3 = 6

n is the number you start with. Undo ÷ 3 by multiplying: 6 × 3 = 18. Check: 18 ÷ 3 = 6.

Answer: n = 18

Example

2400 + □ = 5000

Undo + 2400 by subtracting: 5000 − 2400 = 2600. Check: 2400 + 2600 = 5000.

Answer: 2600

Write an equation for a story

Use a box or a letter for the number you do not know. Joining is +, taking away is −, equal groups are ×, and sharing equally is ÷.

Example

56 chairs are put in 7 equal rows. How many chairs are in each row?

Equation: 7 × r = 56. Use the inverse: r = 56 ÷ 7 = 8. Check: 7 × 8 = 56.

Answer: 8 chairs

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
6 + 4 = □ + 5, so □ = 1010 is the left side. □ + 5 = 10, so □ = 5
□ + 36 = 90, so □ = 126 (90 + 36)Use the inverse: 90 − 36 = 54
4 × □ = 28, so □ = 112 (28 × 4)Use the inverse: 28 ÷ 4 = 7
n ÷ 3 = 6, so n = 2 (6 ÷ 3)Undo ÷ 3 by multiplying: 6 × 3 = 18
4 × □ = 28, so □ = 24 (28 − 4)× is undone by ÷, not by −
4 × 5 = 20 + 6 = 26Write two equations: 4 × 5 = 20, then 20 + 6 = 26

faq.q: What are one-step equations in Grade 4 math in BC?
faq.a: They are equations like □ + 36 = 90, 4 × □ = 28 or n ÷ 3 = 6 with one unknown number. The BC Grade 4 Patterning standard asks students to solve them using all four operations.
Use the inverse operation. Division undoes multiplication, so □ = 28 ÷ 4 = 7. Check by putting 7 back in: 4 × 7 = 28.

faq.q: What does the equal sign mean in Grade 4 math?
faq.a: The equal sign means “is the same as”, not “the answer is”. In 6 + 4 = □ + 5, both sides must be 10, so the box is 5.

faq.q: Are equations on the Grade 4 FSA?
faq.a: The FSA numeracy section checks math skills and problem solving from the BC curriculum. Writing and solving simple equations for word problems, like the ones here, is good practice for it.

sets.title: The equal sign means “the same as”

items.q: The pans balance. Which equation matches?
items.e: The pans balance, so both sides have the same value. The left pan has 6 + 7 and the right pan has 13, so 6 + 7 = 13. The = sign can sit between any two things that are the same.

items.q: The pans balance. Which equation matches?
items.e: The pans balance, so both sides have the same value. The left pan has 24 and the right pan has 4 × 6, so 24 = 4 × 6. The = sign can sit between any two things that are the same.

items.q: The pans balance. Which equation matches?
items.e: The pans balance. 3 × 4 = 12 and 6 + 6 = 12, so 3 × 4 = 6 + 6. The = sign means “is the same as”.

items.q: The pans balance. Which equation matches?
items.e: The pans balance. 20 ÷ 4 = 5 and 10 − 5 = 5, so 20 ÷ 4 = 10 − 5. The = sign means “is the same as”.

items.q:
The pans balance.
What number goes in the box?
items.e: The pans balance, so the box has the same value as 8 × 3. 8 × 3 = 24. Not 11: that adds 8 and 3.

items.q:
The pans balance.
What number goes in the box?
items.e: The box must be the same as 45 ÷ 5. 45 ÷ 5 = 9. Not 40: that subtracts. Not 225: that multiplies.

items.e: 400 − 150 = 250. Not 550: that adds. Not 350: that takes the smaller digit from the larger instead of regrouping.

The pans balance.
What number goes in the box?
items.e: The box is the same as 6 × 7 = 42. Not 13: that adds. Not 36 or 48: those are 6 × 6 and 6 × 8.

items.q: Which equation is true?
items.e: Work out both sides. 5 × 4 = 20 and 10 + 10 = 20, so 5 × 4 = 10 + 10 is true. 5 × 4 = 20 + 10 is false: 20 + 10 is 30.

items.q: Which equation is true? The total can come first.
items.e: 9 × 4 = 36, so 36 = 9 × 4 is true. The total can come first, before the = sign. 6 × 7 is 42, not 36.

items.q: Work out both sides. Which equation is true?
items.e: 18 ÷ 3 = 6 and 2 × 3 = 6, so 18 ÷ 3 = 2 × 3 is true. Both sides are 6. 18 ÷ 3 = 15 is false: 15 is 18 − 3.

items.q: Which equation is true? Check both sides.
Which has the same value as 2 × 6?
items.e: 2 × 6 = 12 and 3 × 4 = 12. They have the same value, so 2 × 6 = 3 × 4.

items.q: Which has the same value as 40 ÷ 5?
items.e: 40 ÷ 5 = 8 and 4 + 4 = 8. They have the same value, so 40 ÷ 5 = 4 + 4.

items.q: Which has the same value as 25 + 37?
items.e: 25 + 37 = 62 and 30 + 32 = 62. They have the same value, so 25 + 37 = 30 + 32.

items.q: Which has the same value as 9 × 5?
items.e: 9 × 5 = 45 and 50 − 5 = 45. They have the same value, so 9 × 5 = 50 − 5.

items.q: What does the = sign mean in 3 × 5 = 10 + 5?
items.e: = means “is the same as”. 3 × 5 = 15 and 10 + 5 = 15, so both sides are the same. It does not just mean “the answer comes next”.

items.q:
□ = 7 × 8
What number goes in the box?
items.e: The = sign can come first. The box is the same as 7 × 8, so it is 56. Not 15: that adds. Not 54 or 64: those are 6 × 9 and 8 × 8.

items.q:
6 + 4 = □ + 5
What number goes in the box?
items.e: The left side is 6 + 4 = 10. So □ + 5 must also be 10, and □ = 5. Not 10: that reads = as “the answer is”. Not 15: that adds all the numbers.

items.q: Liam multiplies 4 by 5, then adds 6. He writes 4 × 5 = 20 + 6 = 26. What is wrong?
items.e: = means both sides are the same. 4 × 5 = 20, but 20 + 6 = 26, so “4 × 5 = 20 + 6” is not true. Liam should write two equations: 4 × 5 = 20 and 20 + 6 = 26.

items.q:
□ + 36 = 90
What number goes in the box?
items.e: Use the inverse. Subtraction undoes addition: □ = 90 − 36 = 54. Check: 54 + 36 = 90. Not 126: that adds, the same operation, instead of subtracting. Not 66: that takes the smaller digit from the larger in each column.

items.q:
□ + 125 = 400
What number goes in the box?
items.e: Use the inverse. Subtraction undoes addition: □ = 400 − 125 = 275. Check: 275 + 125 = 400. Not 525: that adds, the same operation, instead of subtracting. Not 325: that takes the smaller digit from the larger in each column.

items.q:
□ + 1250 = 3000
What number goes in the box?
items.e: Use the inverse. Subtraction undoes addition: □ = 3000 − 1250 = 1750. Check: 1750 + 1250 = 3000. Not 4250: that adds, the same operation, instead of subtracting. Not 2250: that takes the smaller digit from the larger in each column.

items.q:
48 + □ = 100
What number goes in the box?
items.e: Use the inverse. Subtraction undoes addition: □ = 100 − 48 = 52. Check: 48 + 52 = 100. Not 148: that adds, the same operation, instead of subtracting.

items.q:
275 + □ = 650
What number goes in the box?
items.e: Use the inverse. Subtraction undoes addition: □ = 650 − 275 = 375. Check: 275 + 375 = 650. Not 925: that adds, the same operation, instead of subtracting. Not 425: that takes the smaller digit from the larger in each column.

items.q:
2400 + □ = 5000
What number goes in the box?
items.e: Use the inverse. Subtraction undoes addition: □ = 5000 − 2400 = 2600. Check: 2400 + 2600 = 5000. Not 7400: that adds, the same operation, instead of subtracting. Not 3400: that takes the smaller digit from the larger in each column.

items.q: n + 17 = 50. What is n?
items.e: Use the inverse. Subtraction undoes addition: n = 50 − 17 = 33. Check: 33 + 17 = 50. Not 67: that adds, the same operation, instead of subtracting. Not 47: that takes the smaller digit from the larger in each column.

Use the inverse. Subtraction undoes addition: k = 6000 − 4500 = 1500. Check: 4500 + 1500 = 6000. Not 10 500: that adds, the same operation, instead of subtracting. Not 2500: that takes the smaller digit from the larger in each column.

items.q:
90 − □ = 35
What number goes in the box?
items.e: 90 take away what leaves 35? □ = 90 − 35 = 55. Check: 90 − 55 = 35. Not 125: that adds the two numbers. Not 65: that takes the smaller digit from the larger in each column.

items.q:
500 − □ = 260
What number goes in the box?
items.e: 500 take away what leaves 260? □ = 500 − 260 = 240. Check: 500 − 240 = 260. Not 760: that adds the two numbers. Not 360: that takes the smaller digit from the larger in each column.

items.q:
3000 − □ = 1750
What number goes in the box?
items.e: 3000 take away what leaves 1750? □ = 3000 − 1750 = 1250. Check: 3000 − 1250 = 1750. Not 4750: that adds the two numbers. Not 2750: that takes the smaller digit from the larger in each column.

items.q: 64 − y = 29. What is y?
items.e: 64 take away what leaves 29? y = 64 − 29 = 35. Check: 64 − 35 = 29. Not 93: that adds the two numbers. Not 45: that takes the smaller digit from the larger in each column.

items.q:
□ − 28 = 46
What number goes in the box?
items.e: The box is the number you start with. Undo − 28 by adding: □ = 46 + 28 = 74. Check: 74 − 28 = 46. Not 18: that subtracts, the same operation, instead of adding. Not 64: that forgets to carry.

items.q:
□ − 350 = 425
What number goes in the box?
items.e: The box is the number you start with. Undo − 350 by adding: □ = 425 + 350 = 775. Check: 775 − 350 = 425. Not 75: that subtracts, the same operation, instead of adding.

items.q:
□ − 1600 = 2400
What number goes in the box?
items.e: The box is the number you start with. Undo − 1600 by adding: □ = 2400 + 1600 = 4000. Check: 4000 − 1600 = 2400. Not 800: that subtracts, the same operation, instead of adding. Not 3000: that forgets to carry.
m is the number you start with. Undo − 140 by adding: m = 360 + 140 = 500. Check: 500 − 140 = 360. Not 220: that subtracts, the same operation, instead of adding. Not 400: that forgets to carry.

p is the number you start with. Undo − 1200 by adding: p = 2800 + 1200 = 4000. Check: 4000 − 1200 = 2800. Not 1600: that subtracts, the same operation, instead of adding. Not 3000: that forgets to carry.

items.q:
80 = □ + 35
What number goes in the box?
items.e: The = sign can come first. □ + 35 = 80, so □ = 80 − 35 = 45. Check: 45 + 35 = 80. Not 115: that adds. Not 55: that takes the smaller digit from the larger.
The = sign can come first. 900 − n = 600, so n = 900 − 600 = 300. Check: 900 − 300 = 600. Not 1500: that adds the two numbers.

items.q: Noah solves n − 25 = 40 and gets n = 15. What did he do wrong?
items.e: 15 − 25 does not give 40. He used the same operation, subtraction, instead of the inverse. Undo − 25 by adding: n = 40 + 25 = 65. Check: 65 − 25 = 40.

items.q:
4 × □ = 28
What number goes in the box?
items.e: Division undoes multiplication: □ = 28 ÷ 4 = 7. Check: 4 × 7 = 28. Not 24: that subtracts. Not 112: that multiplies, the same operation, instead of dividing.

items.q:
6 × □ = 54
What number goes in the box?
items.e: Division undoes multiplication: □ = 54 ÷ 6 = 9. Check: 6 × 9 = 54. Not 48: that subtracts. Not 324: that multiplies, the same operation, instead of dividing.

items.q: 8 × n = 72. What is n?
items.e: Division undoes multiplication: n = 72 ÷ 8 = 9. Check: 8 × 9 = 72. Not 64: that subtracts. Not 576: that multiplies, the same operation, instead of dividing.

items.q:
□ × 7 = 42
What number goes in the box?
items.e: Division undoes multiplication: □ = 42 ÷ 7 = 6. Check: 6 × 7 = 42. Not 35: that subtracts. Not 294: that multiplies, the same operation, instead of dividing.

items.q:
□ × 5 = 45
What number goes in the box?
items.e: Division undoes multiplication: □ = 45 ÷ 5 = 9. Check: 9 × 5 = 45. Not 40: that subtracts. Not 225: that multiplies, the same operation, instead of dividing.

items.q: k × 3 = 24. What is k?
items.e: Division undoes multiplication: k = 24 ÷ 3 = 8. Check: 8 × 3 = 24. Not 21: that subtracts. Not 72: that multiplies, the same operation, instead of dividing.

items.q:
9 × □ = 63
What number goes in the box?
items.e: Division undoes multiplication: □ = 63 ÷ 9 = 7. Check: 9 × 7 = 63. Not 54: that subtracts. Not 567: that multiplies, the same operation, instead of dividing.

items.q: n ÷ 3 = 6. What is n?
items.e: n is the number you start with. Multiplication undoes division: n = 6 × 3 = 18. Check: 18 ÷ 3 = 6. Not 2: that divides again, the same operation, instead of multiplying.

items.q:
□ ÷ 4 = 7
What number goes in the box?
items.e: The box is the number you start with. Multiplication undoes division: □ = 7 × 4 = 28. Check: 28 ÷ 4 = 7. Not 11: that adds the two numbers.

items.q:
□ ÷ 9 = 6
What number goes in the box?
items.e: The box is the number you start with. Multiplication undoes division: □ = 6 × 9 = 54. Check: 54 ÷ 9 = 6. Not 15: that adds the two numbers.

items.q: t ÷ 2 = 8. What is t?
items.e: t is the number you start with. Multiplication undoes division: t = 8 × 2 = 16. Check: 16 ÷ 2 = 8. Not 4: that divides again, the same operation, instead of multiplying.

items.q:
56 ÷ □ = 7
What number goes in the box?
items.e: Ask: 56 shared into how many groups gives 7 in each? □ = 56 ÷ 7 = 8. Check: 56 ÷ 8 = 7. Not 392: that multiplies. Not 49: that subtracts.

items.q: 36 ÷ n = 4. What is n?
items.e: Ask: 36 shared into how many groups gives 4 in each? n = 36 ÷ 4 = 9. Check: 36 ÷ 9 = 4. Not 144: that multiplies. Not 32: that subtracts.

items.q:
30 ÷ □ = 6
What number goes in the box?
items.e: Ask: 30 shared into how many groups gives 6 in each? □ = 30 ÷ 6 = 5. Check: 30 ÷ 5 = 6. Not 180: that multiplies. Not 24: that subtracts.

items.q:
48 = 6 × □
What number goes in the box?
items.e: The = sign can come first. 6 × □ = 48, so □ = 48 ÷ 6 = 8. Check: 6 × 8 = 48. Not 42: that subtracts. Not 288: that multiplies.

items.q: 9 = n ÷ 7. What is n?
items.e: The = sign can come first. n ÷ 7 = 9, so n = 9 × 7 = 63. Check: 63 ÷ 7 = 9. Not 16: that adds. Not 56: that is 8 × 7.

items.q:
The bar shows 4 equal parts that make 32. 4 × □ = 32
What number goes in the box?
items.e: 4 equal parts make 32, so □ = 32 ÷ 4 = 8. Check: 4 × 8 = 32. Not 28: that subtracts. Not 128: that multiplies.

items.q: The bar shows 5 equal parts of 9. n ÷ 5 = 9. What is n?
items.e: n is the whole. Put the 5 parts together: n = 9 × 5 = 45. Check: 45 ÷ 5 = 9. Not 14: that adds. Not 4: that subtracts.

items.q:
7 × □ = 70
What number goes in the box?
items.e: 7 × 10 = 70, so □ = 70 ÷ 7 = 10. Not 63: that subtracts. Not 490: that multiplies. Not 1: 7 × 1 is 7, not 70.

items.q: Simran solves n ÷ 6 = 3 and gets n = 2. What did she do wrong?
items.e: 2 ÷ 6 is not 3. She used the same operation, division, instead of the inverse. Undo ÷ 6 by multiplying: n = 3 × 6 = 18. Check: 18 ÷ 6 = 3.

sets.title: Write an equation for a story

items.q: Zara has 28 hockey cards. She gets some more. Now she has 64. Which equation matches?
items.e: Zara starts with 28, gets an unknown number more and ends with 64: 28 + □ = 64. 28 + 64 = □ is wrong: 64 is the total, not a part. Then □ = 64 − 28 = 36.

items.q: There are 45 bald eagles in the trees near Squamish. Some fly away. Now 18 are left. Which equation matches?
items.e: Start with 45, take away an unknown number and 18 are left: 45 − □ = 18. Then □ = 45 − 18 = 27.

items.q: A box has 6 bags of granola bars. Each bag has the same number of bars, n. There are 48 bars in all. Which equation matches?
items.e: 6 equal groups of n make 48: 6 × n = 48. Equal groups mean ×, not +. Then n = 48 ÷ 6 = 8.

items.q: 32 students make 4 equal soccer teams. Let t be the number on each team. Which equation matches?
items.e: Sharing 32 into 4 equal teams is division: 32 ÷ 4 = t. So t = 8. 32 × 4 = t would make the teams bigger than the class.

items.q: Lucas has some money. He spends $12 at the PNE and has $25 left. Which equation matches?
items.e: The unknown is the money at the start. Take away $12 and $25 is left: □ − 12 = 25. Then □ = 25 + 12 = $37. 25 − 12 = □ uses the wrong operation.

items.q: A BC Ferries boat has c cars on it. Then 140 more cars drive on. Now there are 400 cars. Which equation matches?
The class puts 56 chairs in 7 equal rows. Let r be the number of chairs in each row. Which equation matches?
items.e: 7 rows of r chairs make 56: 7 × r = 56. Then r = 56 ÷ 7 = 8.

items.q: Chloe shares some Okanagan cherries equally into 5 bags. Each bag has 9 cherries. Let c be the number of cherries at the start. Which equation matches?
items.e: Start with c, share into 5 bags and get 9 in each: c ÷ 5 = 9. Then c = 9 × 5 = 45.

items.q: Which equation means “a number times 8 is 64”?
items.e: Let n be the number. “Times 8” is × 8 and “is 64” is = 64: n × 8 = 64. Then n = 8.

items.q: Which equation means “a number divided by 4 is 7”?
items.e: Start with the number n and divide it by 4: n ÷ 4 = 7. Then n = 7 × 4 = 28. 4 ÷ n starts with 4, not with the number.

items.q: Which equation means “a number plus 250 is 900”?
A Grade 4 class has raised $320 for the Terry Fox Run. The goal is $500. Let m be the money they still need. Which equation matches?
items.e: What they have plus what they still need makes the goal: 320 + m = 500. Then m = 500 − 320 = $180.

items.q: Each chair on a ski lift at Whistler holds 4 people. 36 people ride up on c full chairs. Which equation matches?
items.e: c chairs with 4 people on each make 36: 4 × c = 36. Then c = 36 ÷ 4 = 9.

items.q: The library has 1500 books. Some are checked out. 1200 books are still on the shelves. Let b be the number checked out. Which equation matches?
items.e: Start with 1500, take away b, and 1200 are left: 1500 − b = 1200. Then b = 300.

items.q: Mateo bakes 3 trays of muffins with 12 muffins on each tray. Let m be the number of muffins in all. Which equation matches?
items.e: 3 equal trays of 12 is 3 × 12 = m. So m = 36. 3 + 12 adds the trays to the muffins.

items.q: Which story matches 24 ÷ 6 = □?
c: There are 24 apples and 6 more. How many in all?
There are 24 apples and 6 are eaten. How many are left?
There are 6 bags with 24 apples in each. How many in all?
24 apples are shared into 6 bags. How many in each bag?
items.e: ÷ means sharing into equal groups. Sharing 24 apples into 6 bags is 24 ÷ 6 = □, so □ = 4. 6 bags of 24 would be 6 × 24.

items.q: Which story matches 5 × □ = 40?
c: 5 friends get the same number of stickers. They get 40 in all. How many each?
Kai has 40 stickers and gives away 5. How many are left?
Kai has 5 stickers and gets 40 more. How many now?
5 friends have 40 stickers each. How many in all?
items.e: 5 equal groups of an unknown number make 40: 5 × □ = 40. Then □ = 40 ÷ 5 = 8.

items.q: Which equation means the same as 9 × □ = 54?
items.e: A letter can take the place of the box. Both stand for the same unknown number: 9 × k = 54. In both, the unknown is 6.

items.q: “48 crayons are shared equally into 6 boxes.” Wei writes 48 + 6 = □. Which equation should he write?
items.e: Shared equally means divide, with the total first: 48 ÷ 6 = □. So □ = 8 crayons in each box.

items.q: Owen has 3 bags of 8 marbles. Nadia has 4 bags with the same number in each bag. They have the same number of marbles. Which equation matches?
items.e: Both totals are the same, so both sides are equal: 3 × 8 = 4 × □. 3 × 8 = 24, so □ = 24 ÷ 4 = 6 marbles.

items.q: A fish counter on a creek on Vancouver Island counts 245 salmon by Monday. By Tuesday the total is 610. How many salmon swam by on Tuesday?
items.e: Equation: 245 + □ = 610. □ = 610 − 245 = 365 salmon. Check: 245 + 365 = 610. Not 855: that adds. Not 435: that takes the smaller digit from the larger in each column.

items.q: A Grade 4 class has raised $185 for the Terry Fox Run. The goal is $400. How much more do they need to raise?
items.e: Equation: 185 + □ = 400. □ = 400 − 185 = $215. Check: $185 + $215 = $400. Not $585: that adds. Not $385: that takes the smaller digit from the larger in each column.

items.q: Ethan’s soccer team shares 54 orange slices equally. There are 9 players. How many slices does each player get?
items.e: Equation: 9 × □ = 54. Use the inverse: 54 ÷ 9 = 6 slices. Check: 9 × 6 = 54. Not 45: that subtracts. Not 486: that multiplies instead of dividing.

items.q: 42 students go on a field trip to Stanley Park. Each van holds 7 students. All the vans are full. How many vans do they need?
items.e: Equation: 7 × v = 42. Use the inverse: 42 ÷ 7 = 6 vans. Check: 7 × 6 = 42. Not 35: that subtracts. Not 294: that multiplies instead of dividing.

items.q: A class visits the Vancouver Aquarium. The teacher splits the students into 4 equal groups. There are 8 students in each group. How many students are in the class?
items.e: Equation: n ÷ 4 = 8. Undo ÷ 4 by multiplying: n = 8 × 4 = 32 students. Check: 32 ÷ 4 = 8. Not 2: that divides again instead of multiplying. Not 12: that adds.

items.q: A ferry can carry 310 cars. 185 cars are already on the ferry. How many more cars can fit?
items.e: Equation: 185 + □ = 310. □ = 310 − 185 = 125 cars. Check: 185 + 125 = 310. Not 495: that adds. Not 275: that takes the smaller digit from the larger in each column.

items.q: A ski hill sells 1250 lift tickets in the morning. By the end of the day it has sold 2000. How many tickets did it sell in the afternoon?
items.e: Equation: 1250 + □ = 2000. □ = 2000 − 1250 = 750 tickets. Check: 1250 + 750 = 2000. Not 3250: that adds. Not 1250: that takes the smaller digit from the larger in each column.

items.q: Ava has some stickers. She gives 35 to friends and has 48 left. How many stickers did she have at the start?
items.e: Equation: □ − 35 = 48. Undo − 35 by adding: □ = 48 + 35 = 83. Check: 83 − 35 = 48. Not 13: that subtracts. Not 73: that forgets to carry the ten.

items.q: Kai reads 8 pages each day. How many days will it take him to read 72 pages?
items.e: Equation: 8 × d = 72. Use the inverse: 72 ÷ 8 = 9 days. Check: 8 × 9 = 72. Not 64: that subtracts. Not 576: that multiplies instead of dividing.

items.q: Sofia plants 56 cedar seedlings in 8 equal rows. How many seedlings are in each row?
items.e: Equation: 8 × r = 56. Use the inverse: 56 ÷ 8 = 7 seedlings. Check: 8 × 7 = 56. Not 48: that subtracts. Not 448: that multiplies instead of dividing.

items.q: The Grouse Grind trail on Grouse Mountain is about 2900 m long. Emma has hiked 1700 m. About how many more metres does she have to hike?
A whale-watching boat in Victoria has 48 seats. 29 people are on the boat. How many seats are empty?
items.e: Equation: 29 + □ = 48. □ = 48 − 29 = 19 seats. Check: 29 + 19 = 48. Not 77: that adds. Not 21: that takes the smaller digit from the larger.

items.q: Arjun buys 4 rolls of hockey tape. Each roll costs the same. He pays $12. How much does each roll cost?
items.e: Equation: 4 × □ = 12. Use the inverse: □ = 12 ÷ 4 = $3. Check: 4 × $3 = $12. Not $8: that subtracts. Not $48: that multiplies.

items.q: A toonie is worth $2. How many toonies make $16?
items.e: Equation: 2 × t = 16. Use the inverse: t = 16 ÷ 2 = 8 toonies. Check: 8 × $2 = $16. Not 14: that subtracts. Not 32: that multiplies.

items.q: 6 friends share some granola bars equally. Each friend gets 3 bars. How many granola bars were there?
items.e: Equation: b ÷ 6 = 3. Undo ÷ 6 by multiplying: b = 3 × 6 = 18 bars. Check: 18 ÷ 6 = 3. Not 2: that divides 6 by 3. Not 9: that adds.

items.q: Harjot’s family drives about 390 km from Vancouver to Kelowna. They have driven 240 km. How far do they still have to drive?
items.e: Equation: 240 + □ = 390. □ = 390 − 240 = 150 km. Check: 240 + 150 = 390. Not 630: that adds instead of subtracting.

items.q: Olivia cuts a 45 cm ribbon into 5 equal pieces. How long is each piece?
items.e: Equation: 5 × □ = 45. Use the inverse: □ = 45 ÷ 5 = 9 cm. Check: 5 × 9 = 45. Not 40: that subtracts. Not 225: that multiplies.

items.q: Ryan needs 80 juice boxes for Sports Day. They come in packs of 10. How many packs does he need?
items.e: Equation: 10 × p = 80. Use the inverse: p = 80 ÷ 10 = 8 packs. Check: 10 × 8 = 80. Not 70: that subtracts. Not 800: that multiplies.

items.q: Hana scores some points in the first half of a basketball game and 18 points in the second half. She scores 45 points in all. How many points did she score in the first half?
items.e: Equation: n + 18 = 45. n = 45 − 18 = 27 points. Check: 27 + 18 = 45. Not 63: that adds. Not 33: that takes the smaller digit from the larger.

items.q: A school wants to collect 2500 cans for the food bank. So far it has 1750 cans. How many more cans does it need?
items.e: Equation: 1750 + □ = 2500. □ = 2500 − 1750 = 750 cans. Check: 1750 + 750 = 2500. Not 4250: that adds. Not 1250: that takes the smaller digit from the larger.
